In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the long-term increase of the total diacid concentrations over the WNP is primarily attributed to the biogenic secondary organic aerosol formation.

the observed diacids and their oxidation products are primarily from the photochemical oxidation of biogenic VOCs from East Asia and the subsequent transport to Chichijima, with a minor contribution from the oxidation of anthropogenic VOCs from the same region.
the long-term trends in the water-soluble diacid and related compounds observed over the WNP were mainly driven by the enhanced photochemical production of biogenic precursors from East Asia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enhanced levels of water-solube diacids in the WNP were primarily due to the aqueous photooxidation of anthropogenic and biogenic volatile organic carbon compounds.
the photooxidation of isoprene and monoterpenes from East Asia is a major source of water-solubledi-carboxylic acids over the WNP.

the long-term observations of the molecular composition of the organic aerosols over the WNP have provided valuable insights into the sources and formation pathways of the organic compounds, and their temporal trends in the western Pacific region.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the concentrations of diacarboxylic acid, ω-oxocarboxylic and α-dicarboxylic compounds in the western North-Pacific aerosol are increasing over the last 12 years, which can be attributed to the long-range transport of biogenic photochemical oxidation products from East Asia.
the photochemical processing of biogenic emissions is the major source of diacids in the WNP, and that this source is increasing with time.
the long-range transported biogenic photochemical products are the major contributors to the water-soluble diacids in marine organic aerosols over the WNP.
